observed_failure.facts: Preserved baseline completed all twelve homing actuators; shutdown logged motor deactivation twice, then terminate called without an active exception from ControlBoardHardwareInterface destruction; process exit -6. Parent reports operator observed relaxed legs. This report did not perform that session.

diagnosis.finding: The exact preserved IMUManager has a joinable thread owner and stop()/join() but no destructor; no driver call to stop() exists. Normal member destruction releases its sensor before destroying the joinable std::thread, whose destructor invokes std::terminate. It also permits destruction of a sensor while a sample is in flight.
diagnosis.confidence: Matching defect reproduced with the exact original production IMU sources and a fake BNO055; consistent with actual shutdown trace. No claim that other driver lifecycle defects are thereby excluded.

production_change: Add IMUManager destructor calling existing stop() before any member is destroyed; initialize its stop flag true before begin. No alteration to BNO055 sampling implementation, driver activation/deactivation, homing loops/gains/targets, policy or calibration.

validation.environment: Existing pinned ROS Jazzy container, --network none --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges; no devices mapped. No ROS node/executor or hardware code is executed by tests.
validation.lifecycle_test_design: Compile actual production IMUManager, replacing only the three BNO055 sensor functions at link time; no rt_bno055.cpp, SPI or I2C linked into test. Five separate CTest processes with ten-second test timeouts.

original.matching_abort_message: terminate called without an active exception

validation.checks: Active destruction joins the sampler; destruction during a deliberately blocked sample waits until its release, then destroys the sensor; explicit stop is idempotent; stop-and-restart remains supported; no sensor/polling thread survives manager destruction.

staging.plan: Root verifies original CMake hash, copies original Pi package into a new separate driver overlay, applies only these pinned files, builds/tests natively without opening hardware, and records library/source identity before considering another explicitly supervised homing/shutdown session. Baseline workspace remains unchanged.

limits: The fake sensor proves thread ownership/ordering, not actual I2C timing or a bound on shutdown latency. stop() joins after an in-progress real sample returns.
This does not add a homing timeout/cancellation path or prove joystick/electrical-stop behavior.
No native Pi patched-library test or repeat physical shutdown has yet been performed.

Existing driver destructor releases its process lock before deactivation, and failed/partial initialization teardown is not covered by this narrowly scoped IMU test; those separate concerns are not silently claimed fixed.
